name: Jupiter
description: Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System — so massive that all other planets could fit inside it with room to spare. It is a gas giant with no solid surface, famous for its Great Red Spot storm and 95 known moons, including four large Galilean moons.
mass: 1.898 × 10^27 kg (317.8 × Earth, 2.5× all other planets combined)
atmosphere: 90% Hydrogen, 10% Helium, trace methane, ammonia, water, hydrogen sulfide
great_red_spot: Storm larger than Earth, active for 400+ years, shrinking in recent decades
magnetic_field: 19.7× stronger than Earth's — strongest of any planet
magnetosphere_size: Extends 3–7 million km sunward, 700+ million km away from the Sun
rings: Faint dust rings discovered 1979 by Voyager 1

notable_moons.Io: Most volcanically active body in the Solar System
notable_moons.Europa: Subsurface ocean — prime candidate for extraterrestrial life
notable_moons.Ganymede: Largest moon in Solar System, bigger than Mercury
notable_moons.Callisto: Heavily cratered, 4 billion years old surface

known_missions: Galileo (NASA, 1995–2003) — orbited Jupiter, studied Galilean moons
Juno (NASA, 2016 — active) — studying atmosphere and interior
summary: Jupiter is the Solar System's giant protector — its immense gravity deflects or captures many asteroids and comets that might otherwise hit inner planets. Its moon Europa, with a subsurface liquid water ocean, is one of the most promising places in the Solar System to search for life beyond Earth.
interesting_facts: Jupiter is so large that all other planets could fit inside it
The Great Red Spot is a storm larger than Earth that has persisted for over 400 years
Jupiter has the shortest day of any planet — one rotation in just 9 hours 55 minutes
Europa's subsurface ocean may contain more liquid water than all of Earth's oceans
Jupiter's moon Ganymede is the largest moon in the Solar System — bigger than Mercury
Io is the most volcanically active body in the Solar System with 400+ active volcanoes
Jupiter emits more heat than it receives from the Sun
Jupiter's magnetic field is 19.7× stronger than Earth's
Jupiter acts as a gravitational shield, protecting Earth from many asteroid impacts
The Europa Clipper mission launched in 2024 will study Europa's potential ocean life

faq.a: Jupiter has a diameter of 139,820 km — 11.2 times Earth's diameter. It's so massive (317.8 Earth masses) that all other planets combined could fit inside it twice over.

faq.q: What is the Great Red Spot?
faq.a: The Great Red Spot is a massive anticyclonic storm in Jupiter's southern hemisphere. It's larger than Earth and has been observed continuously for over 400 years, though it has been shrinking in recent decades.

faq.q: Does Jupiter have a solid surface?
faq.a: No. Jupiter is a gas giant — there is no solid surface. Its atmosphere gradually becomes denser and hotter as you go deeper, transitioning to a liquid hydrogen layer and possibly a rocky/metallic core.

Europa is a top candidate for extraterrestrial life. Its subsurface ocean (liquid water under an ice shell, kept liquid by Jupiter's tidal heating) could potentially support microbial life similar to deep-sea environments on Earth.

faq.q: How many moons does Jupiter have?
faq.a: Jupiter has 95 confirmed moons as of 2024, more than any other planet. The four largest (Galilean moons) — Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto — were discovered by Galileo in 1610.

faq.q: How long does it take Jupiter to orbit the Sun?
faq.a: Jupiter takes 11.86 Earth years to complete one orbit around the Sun, at an average distance of 778.5 million km (5.2 AU).

faq.q: What is Juno doing at Jupiter?
faq.a: NASA's Juno spacecraft has been orbiting Jupiter since 2016, studying its atmosphere, magnetic field, interior structure, and polar regions. Its mission has been extended multiple times to study Jupiter's moons.

Jupiter's colorful bands are alternating zones (pale) and belts (dark) of cloud layers at different altitudes and wind speeds. The different colors reflect different chemical compositions (ammonia ice, ammonium hydrosulfide, water).
Jupiter's gravity is 24.79 m/s² — 2.53 times Earth's gravity. A 70 kg person would weigh about 177 kg on Jupiter (if there were a surface to stand on).

Jupiter's massive gravity acts as a shield, deflecting or capturing asteroids and comets that might otherwise impact the inner planets. This 'Jupiter Effect' is thought to have made Earth safer for life to develop.
